methodological_rigor.justification: The authors assemble 1,294 cfMeDIP-seq samples across 11 cancer types with uniform MEDIPIPE processing, rigorous QC (21 metrics), ComBat-seq+DESeq2 batch correction, and thoughtful mitigation of confounders including age, sex, PBL contamination via in-silico depletion, and SE/PE sequencing differences. They restrict DMR discovery to baseline time points to avoid pseudo-replication, apply PBL-depleted bin filtering, and exclude blood/endothelial cell-associated regions. Statistical treatment is exemplary: FDR (BH) correction throughout, nested cross-validation with per-fold PCA fitted only on training data to prevent leakage, power analysis via PERMANOVA/adonis2 with 999 permutations, Cohen's d sensitivity analysis, and appropriate nonparametric tests (Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc) where normality was violated. Independent validation in 220 samples including 3 unseen cancer types strengthens generalization claims; limitations (missing age/sex for >240 samples, HCC protocol differences affecting motifs) are explicitly acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective pooled analysis of convenience cohorts from nine cfMeDIP-seq studies plus validation samples from two additional studies—functionally a case-series/low-quality cohort compilation, which maps to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is high: the classifiers achieve mAUC 0.954-0.986 on independent validation with sensitivity of 76.6-93.0% at 99% specificity, compared favorably to GRAIL (54.9% at 99.3%) and cfMethyl-seq (80.7% at 97.9%), and demonstrate multicancer detection including three types absent from the training data. The resource itself (uniformly processed pancancer cfDNA methylome/fragmentome compendium) directly informs near-term biomarker development and screening assay design. However, no prospective clinical validation or patient-relevant endpoints (survival, treatment change) are reported, keeping it short of practice-changing status.

reporting_quality.justification: As a multivariable prediction model development and validation study, TRIPOD is the most applicable standard; the manuscript covers most TRIPOD items including participant selection, predictor definitions, outcome, sample size justification via formal power analysis, handling of missing data (exclusion of samples lacking age/sex for confounder analyses), model development with nested CV and hyperparameter tuning, independent external validation with performance metrics (AUC, sensitivity at fixed specificity), and calibration-adjacent reporting. A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Source Data for all main and most extended figures are listed, supplementary tables cover DMRs/motifs/samples, and MEDIPIPE is an open pipeline previously published—suggesting data/code availability is strong, though repository URLs were REDACTED in the normalized text so I cannot verify direct deposition. Minor gaps include limited reporting on calibration curves and decision-analytic metrics.

novelty_literature.justification: The work positions itself as the largest compiled pancancer cfMeDIP-seq cohort (n=1,294) and the first integrated pancancer analysis combining cfDNA methylome and fragmentome (5' motifs, fragment ratios, nucleosome footprints, insert size) derived from a single assay. The identification of 14,202 common pancancer hyper-DMRs, cancer-specific signatures across 11 types, and the demonstration that fragmentomic features of methylated fragments add discriminatory value over methylation alone fills a documented gap (individual methods exist in prior cfDNA WGS work by Cristiano, Jiang, Vanderstichele, Mouliere, Snyder). Novelty is substantial but incremental rather than field-defining: each constituent technique was previously published and the underlying datasets (TCGE cohorts) were individually reported; the contribution is integration, harmonization, and scale. Guarding against novelty leniency, this is a 4 rather than 5.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear Methods-Results-Discussion flow, dense but readable prose, and effective use of subsections (data processing, confounder mitigation, DMR identification, fragmentomics, classification, subtype analysis). Figures 1-5 are logically sequenced from data overview through signature discovery to classifier performance, with informative legends reporting exact sample sizes and statistical tests. Tables and extended data figures are consistently cross-referenced. Minor weaknesses: some Methods paragraphs are information-dense and could be tightened (e.g., the overlapping pancancer/cancer-specific DMR filtering logic), and the discussion is relatively brief given the scope. Overall publication-ready with minor copy-editing needed.

key_strengths: Largest harmonized pancancer cfMeDIP-seq compendium to date (n=1,294) with uniform MEDIPIPE processing and rigorous batch correction (ComBat-seq+DESeq2) separating SE/PE sequencing modes
Thorough confounder mitigation: in-silico PBL depletion, exclusion of age/sex-associated and blood/endothelial cell-associated regions, baseline-only DMR discovery to avoid pseudo-replication
Exemplary ML methodology with nested cross-validation, PCA fitted only on training folds to prevent leakage, formal PERMANOVA-based multivariate power analysis, and Cohen's d sensitivity analysis

Independent validation in 220 samples including 3 cancer types absent from training, with performance (mAUC 0.954-0.986; 76.6-93.0% sensitivity at 99% specificity) competitive with GRAIL and cfMethyl-seq benchmarks
Integrated methylome+fragmentome analysis from a single cfMeDIP-seq assay demonstrates added discriminatory value of 5' end motifs and fragment ratios for cancer-type and subtype classification
key_concerns: Oxford LoE 4 retrospective pooled convenience cohort with no prospective clinical validation or patient outcomes; practice-changing claims cannot be made from this design
Age and sex records missing for >240 samples forced their exclusion as covariates in main analyses, with confounder consistency shown only across subsets where data were available
HCC validation healthy controls showed protocol-related 5' motif baseline shifts that degraded motif-containing classifier performance, highlighting residual batch/protocol sensitivity
Melanoma validation accuracy was only 33.3% (n=9) and some subtype comparisons (hemangiopericytoma n=3) are severely underpowered despite reported performance
Fragmentomic readouts are restricted to methylation-enriched fragments by design and may not capture genome-wide fragmentation biology, limiting generalization to cfMeDIP-seq-specific contexts
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically rigorous, large-scale resource paper with solid independent validation and competitive classifier performance, but constrained to Oxford LoE 4 by its retrospective pooled design and without prospective clinical endpoints; this places it comfortably within Tier 2 (high-quality translational work in the Nature Communications / Clinical Cancer Research / JCO Precision Oncology band) with minor revisions needed around underpowered subgroups and protocol-related motif drift.
